items: Calcium carbonate (limestone, marble, chalk) is a building material and is used in cement, concrete, and as a filler in paper and plastics.
Quicklime (CaO) and slaked lime (Ca(OH)2) are used to make cement, mortar and plaster; quicklime also removes impurities in steel making.
Gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O) is used to make plasterboard (drywall) and plaster of Paris (CaSO4.1/2H2O).
Calcium oxide and calcium carbonate are used in flue-gas desulphurisation (wet scrubbing) to remove acidic sulphur dioxide from power-station emissions, preventing acid rain.
Magnesium oxide is used as a refractory material for lining furnaces because of its high melting point.

blocks.title: Did you know?
blocks.text: Magnesium metal is used in lightweight alloys for aircraft and cars, and in fireworks and flares for its bright light. Strontium compounds give red colours in fireworks and flares. Beryllium strengthens alloys (springs, aerospace parts) and is used in X-ray tubes because X-rays pass through it.
